title: Compact hero with modular banners and step-rail for Quickstart landing
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a compact, developer-focused Quickstart landing hero that uses modular banners (contextual calls-to-action) and a horizontal step-rail to surface the 3-step onboarding flow. Deliver visual assets, microcopy variants for developer vs enterprise personas, and a screenshot pipeline for automated crops and blurred/annotated overlays for docs and release notes.
acceptance_criteria: Hero layout fits 1280x720, 1024x576 and mobile breakpoints without content overlap
Three modular banners (Try, Integrate, Observe) are tokenized components in Figma with responsive constraints
Step-rail shows progressive disclosure: collapsed mobile -> expanded desktop; accessible via keyboard and screen-readers
Microcopy variants documented and approved by PM for both 'developer' and 'platform' audiences
Screenshot generation script accepted by engineering (example PR linked) and produces three device crops per state
All assets uploaded to Drive + Figma and referenced in the PRD; UX review signed off by design lead
decisions: Use a 12-column grid with 16px gutters; hero content constrained to 960px center column
Make banners modular components that can be reordered by PMs in the CMS
Step-rail will use progressive disclosure: show icons+titles on mobile, reveal descriptions on hover/focus on tablet+
Primary CTA tone: conversational imperative for devs ("Try in 2 mins"); enterprise variant: "Request a demo or dedicated trial"
Use soft motion (120ms ease-in) for step-rail transitions to reduce perceived latency without distracting streaming demo
design_notes: Avoid illustrative hero characters — prioritize schematic diagrams that map to Redwood concepts (runtime -> routing -> console). Provide 3 microcopy tiers (concise, explanatory, enterprise) and mark which variant appears per experiment. Ensure color tokens match global theme (token names included in Figma). Annotate screenshot overlays with callouts (red boxes) and step numbers to match step-rail. Provide accessible color contrast >= 4.5:1 for key text.
progress_updates: 2025-11-03: Kickoff meeting with PM and ENG; aligned on goals and success metrics (CTR on Try CTA, time-to-first-request)
2025-11-05: Exploratory comps created — three layout directions (stacked, split, compact-centered). Shared Figma link; initial preference for compact-centered.
2025-11-07: Design critique — engineering flagged concerns about screenshot pipeline and suggested a small helper script for consistent crops; added dependency ENG-2115.
2025-11-09: Microcopy variants drafted; PM requested an enterprise-focused CTA variant and security microcopy blurb (GDPR/HSM callout) — updated designs.
2025-11-11: Accessibility review pass; keyboard flows for step-rail validated by accessibility engineer; small focus outline tweak planned.
2025-11-12: Uploaded final Figma components (v1.3) and exported annotated screenshot set; opened PR to console repo for screenshot script: #4821
next_steps: Finalize device crops and hand off screenshot script to ENG for integration (ENG owner: Raj Patel)
Run A/B test variant with 'concise' vs 'enterprise' microcopy for two weeks post-launch
Coordinate with Docs to swap in annotated screenshots for the Quickstart guide release notes
Prepare export bundle for Marketing: hero animation GIF + static banners + step-rail SVGs
notes_for_engineering: Screenshot script should accept a state JSON (hero/banner/step index), output three crops (desktop/tablet/mobile) and a blurred-background variant for GDPR-sensitive screenshots. Include metadata file with token names and microcopy variant used.
ux_risks: Step-rail could be misinterpreted as navigation; mitigated by clear ARIA roles and persistent step numbers in the screenshot overlays
